doc.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023

title: Gene Bertoncini: faith, weddings and integrity
summary: Rowe quotes Bertoncini on gifts; Bailey says he calls a music career an act of faith and plays every gig with the same integrity, citing Joan Rivers.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I understand Gene Bertoncini was an important person for you.

Yes. I was able to interview him back in 2001 and I wanted to share maybe one or two brief quotes. And I had asked him why jazz, what turned him on. And he said, “I don’t quite understand why you are drawn to a particular work or a particular art. I consider it all a gift, the gift of being drawn to the music and wanting to learn that music, a gift of a particular instrument. It’s all something we don’t really have choices about. I get irritated at people who think they’ve created their own gift instead of recognizing that it’s really something else at play.”
Yeah what is that something else I wonder, for him? Do you know if he’s like a man of faith or is there something —

Yeah well I would say he is. I mean I don’t know specifically what faith but I remember meeting him and hanging out with him in my early days in New York. And he would always just say, “A career in music? It’s an act of faith.”
And it’s true. It is true. You’re like well I have a gig next month? Well I have to trust that I will.

You know I felt so naive for a long time thinking about how jazz musicians live and make a living. And I recall — he must have just said it in passing after our interview — about you know, “Yeah well like tomorrow I’m playing a wedding.” And I’m thinking Gene Bertoncini plays weddings. And after hearing that from a lot of musicians, well of course I do that, would you rather I wait tables or something? And it was very informative to realize that.

Um hum. Yeah well you know what’s a great — on a different art form, stand-up comedy is Joan Rivers. I recommend this movie, “Joan Rivers: A Piece of Work.” That first twenty minutes of that movie really shows a working freelance artist. That woman hustled gigs to the day she died. And you know she was like sometimes you’re playing at the biggest hall in Vegas or whatever and you’ve got a long one, sometimes you’re doing a bar mitzvah. You do everything with the same integrity. They’re not different — and I know that with Gene. If he’s playing a wedding or a birthday party, he’s playing with the same integrity that he does if he’s playing at Carnegie Hall. That’s your professional acumen. That’s what you bring to everything. You know you don’t go ah, I’m going to play for a bunch of loons over here. You would never do that I guess because it is that thing of every time you get a chance to play or perform it is a gift. It really is a gift that you’re sharing. Not everybody gets to do that and see what we see.
